course_name_original: Sistemas Mecatrónicos de un Grado de Libertad
prerequisites: Knowledge of theory of machines and mechanisms at degree level
Knowledge of automatic regulation at degree level

learning_outcomes.text: Develop technical specifications to pose a problem in mechatronic engineering maintaining a global and integrative vision and using prescriptive, procedural or performance specifications as appropriate.

Evaluate the feasibility of new mechatronic products, based on their technological characteristics, manufacturing possibilities and other socio-economic factors related to their possible implementation.

Students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students possess the learning skills that will allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
Identify the subcomponents of a technologically complex system, the interactions between them, and the effects and consequences of their possible redesign.
Discriminate the most critical components in a mechatronic system and justify their possible redesign from the point of view of the control system.
Acquire knowledge about the characteristic properties of the main types of materials.
Recognize and calculate the different types of internal stresses in sections of resistant elements.
Students will be able to perform kinematic and dynamic simulations of mechanisms.
Students will be able to understand the need to jointly design mechanical components and the control system as strongly coupled elements.
Students will be able to parameterize a simple movement according to its specifications.

syllabus_topics: Kinematics and dynamics of simple mechanisms
assessment_rules: For the ordinary January call, the assessment is based on a written test (30%), coursework (60%), and an aptitude scale (10%). The written test is an individual exam, which can be multiple-choice, theoretical questions, or short problem-solving, on paper or via Virtual Campus. Coursework can be individual and/or group, evaluating technical and formal aspects. For extraordinary calls in May and June, and differentiated assessment, evaluation will be based on the written test and coursework with the same weights.
